Reproducing Watson et al. (2016) on DANDI:000041 and CRCNS:fcx-1¶

Paper. Watson BO, Levenstein D, Greene JP, Gelinas JN, Buzsáki G (2016). Network homeostasis and state dynamics of neocortical sleep. Neuron 90, 839-852. doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2016.03.036.

Claims. claims/watson-2016.yaml, written from the accepted author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC4873379) with its supplement 1 (Table S1, Figures S1 to S5 legends, Supplemental Experimental Procedures) and supplement 2. Every claim lists both datasets, and each is tested on each, except fig5c-wake-movement, tested on CRCNS only as DANDI holds no motion or EMG signal.

Datasets.

  • DANDI:000041, version 0.261104.0300 (doi:10.48324/dandi.000041/0.261104.0300), 22 NWB files, streamed with remfile and h5py. The paper cites no version. This is the most recent published version; its release notes say that all files were re-converted from the lab's source files, correcting the unit table and its cell-type labels, the spike times of Dino-072114 and the LFP gain, all of which the analysis uses, so no earlier version describes the paper's data better. The draft (modified 2026-11-06) is not used, as it can change.
  • CRCNS:fcx-1 (doi:10.6080/K02N506Q), not versioned: the 27 session tar.gz files under fcx-1/live/data/ of the public bucket, each streamed once over parallel range requests and decompressed as it arrives; the MD5 sums from the data set's checksums.md5 of the files read are printed below.

How the two datasets differ. CRCNS:fcx-1 holds the lab's own state intervals (WAKE, SLEEP, WAKE-SLEEP cycles, packets, MAs, REM, WAKE interruptions), its UP/DOWN and spindle detections, and motion; those are used as deposited (reading a of the claims). DANDI:000041 holds Awake, Non-REM and REM epochs only, so the paper's intervals are built from them by the rules of Table S1, and UP/DOWN states and spindles are detected here (reading b). Both hold the LFP; band powers are computed here for both from the lab's spindle/good channel.

Outcome per claim. One outcome is given per claim, judged on CRCNS:fcx-1, which holds all 27 sessions, the lab's own cell classification (_CellIDs, which gives the paper's 995 pE and 126 pI) and the lab's own state intervals, UP/DOWN states and spindles, so it holds the data the paper's tests used. DANDI:000041 holds 22 of the sessions, cell-type labels that differ from the lab's in 7 of them, and Awake, Non-REM and REM epochs only, from which the paper's intervals are rebuilt here; its result is stated beside each CRCNS result, and where it differs the section says so. This is a choice of this attempt (the protocol gives one outcome per claim and the claims file sets no rule for two datasets). In round 1 a claim was reproduced only when it held on both datasets; the verifier pointed out that the claims file has no such rule and that DANDI's differences come from what it lacks.

import time, resource
import numpy as np
import watson as W
t_load = time.time()
D = {}
D["000041"] = W.load_dataset("000041", workers=2)
t_dandi = time.time() - t_load
D["crcns-fcx-1"] = W.load_dataset("crcns-fcx-1", workers=3)
print(f"loaded DANDI in {t_dandi/60:.1f} min, CRCNS in {(time.time()-t_load-t_dandi)/60:.1f} min; peak memory of this process "
      f"{resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss/1e6:.2f} GB")
print("DANDI assets read (version", W.DANDI_VERSION + "):")
for p, a, sz in W.dandi_assets():
    print(f"  {p}  {sz/1e9:.2f} GB  asset {a}")
md5 = W.crcns_checksums()
print("CRCNS files read, with their MD5 from checksums.md5:")
for n in W.CRCNS_SESSIONS:
    print(f"  data/{n}.tar.gz  {md5.get('data/' + n + '.tar.gz')}")

Data check¶

Counts by subject and session, units, state intervals, events, ranges of times, the channel count of each CRCNS LFP stream against its .xml, and a check that spikes, states and UP states share a clock: population spikes rise sharply at UP onsets and not when the onsets are shifted by 30 minutes.

In [2]:
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
import watson as W
DS = ["000041", "crcns-fcx-1"]
STATES = ["wake", "nrem", "rem"]
def pr(*a):
    print(*a)
def fmt(x, n=3):
    return "nan" if x is None or not np.isfinite(x) else f"{x:.{n}g}"
def rp(res):
    return "; ".join(f"{k}: R={fmt(v[0])}, p={fmt(v[1])}, n={v[2]}" for k, v in res.items())
def nancorr(a, b):
    ok = np.isfinite(a) & np.isfinite(b)
    return np.corrcoef(a[ok], b[ok])[0, 1] if ok.sum() > 2 else np.nan
def cells_of(s, kind):
    return s["E"] if kind == "E" else s["I"]

for ds in DS:
    ss = D[ds]
    pr(f"== {ds}: {len(ss)} sessions, rats {sorted(set(s['rat'] for s in ss))}")
    for s in ss:
        I = s["ints"]
        sp = s.get("spindles")
        pr(f"{s['name']:18s} rat={s['rat']:9s} units={len(s['spikes']):3d} pE={len(s['E']):3d} pI={len(s['I']):2d} "
           f"cycles={len(s['cycles'])} packets={len(I['SWSPacket'])} MA={len(I['MA'])} REM={len(I['REM'])} "
           f"UP={len(s.get('up', []))} DOWN={len(s.get('dn', []))} spindles={0 if sp is None else len(sp['start'])} "
           f"LFP={'yes' if 'bp_delta' in s['G'] else 'no'} last spike={max(x.max() for x in s['spikes'] if len(x)):.0f} s "
           f"LFP length={s.get('lfp_seconds', 0):.0f} s")
    allsp = np.concatenate([np.concatenate(s['spikes']) for s in ss])
    pr("spike times: min", allsp.min(), "max", allsp.max(), "s; fraction of times that are whole seconds",
       np.mean(allsp == np.round(allsp)))
    lab = [s["ctype"] for s in ss]
    pr("cell types:", {k: int(sum((l == k).sum() for l in lab)) for k in ["E", "I", "?"]})
    if ds == "crcns-fcx-1":
        pr("channels: .xml against the count found from the .eeg stream where the .xml came later:",
           [(s["name"], s["nch_xml"], s["nch_guess"]) for s in ss if s["nch_guess"]])
        pr("LFP sampling rate in _BasicMetaData:", sorted(set(s["lfp_rate_xml"] for s in ss)))
        pr("LFP length against last state interval end (s):",
           [(s["name"], round(s["lfp_seconds"]), round(max(np.max(np.asarray(c['sleep'])) for c in s['cycles']))) for s in ss][:5], "...")
        pr("spindle amplitude range (uV):", np.percentile(np.concatenate([s['spindles']['amp_uV'] for s in ss]), [0, 50, 100]))
    else:
        pr("LFP rate:", sorted(set(s.get("lfp_rate", np.nan) for s in ss)), "sessions without LFP:", [s["name"] for s in ss if not s.get("have_lfp")])
        pr("regions of units:", {k: int(sum((s['region'] == k).sum() for s in ss)) for k in sorted(set(np.concatenate([s['region'] for s in ss])))})
        pr("electrode locations:", sorted(set(np.concatenate([s['electrode_location'] for s in ss]))))
        pr("LFP starting_time (s), distinct values over files with LFP:", sorted(set(s.get("lfp_starting_time", np.nan) for s in ss if s.get("have_lfp"))),
           "(added to the LFP window times and LFP detections)")
        pr("acquisition series per file (name, shape, rate):", sorted(set(str(s.get("acquisition")) for s in ss)),
           "; the only ElectricalSeries with data is the 1250 Hz LFP (rate above), so no wideband signal for an EMG")
    # clock check: rate of pE cells is higher in WAKE than nonREM? and UP-state onsets align with
    # population spiking, labels shifted by 30 min break the alignment
    on, off = [], []
    for s in ss:
        up = np.asarray(s.get('up', np.zeros((0, 2))))
        if len(up) < 50:
            continue
        mua = np.sort(np.concatenate([s['spikes'][i] for i in s['E']]))
        for shift, lst in [(0.0, on), (1800.0, off)]:
            st = up[:, 0] + shift
            c1 = np.searchsorted(mua, st + 0.1) - np.searchsorted(mua, st)
            c0 = np.searchsorted(mua, st) - np.searchsorted(mua, st - 0.1)
            lst.append((c1.sum() + 1) / (c0.sum() + 1))
    pr("population spikes 0-100 ms after over 100-0 ms before UP onsets, median over sessions:",
       fmt(np.median(on)), "; with UP onsets shifted by 1800 s:", fmt(np.median(off)))
    # LFP clock: delta power in nonREM packets against WAKE, with the state intervals as scored and
    # shifted by 1800 s (a contrast a clock offset between the LFP and the state table would remove)
    on, off = [], []
    for s in ss:
        if "bp_delta" not in s["G"] or not s["cycles"]: continue
        lp = np.log(s["G"]["bp_delta"])
        for shift, lst in [(0, on), (1800, off)]:
            kn = W.secs(W.state_pieces(s, "nrem") + shift); kw = W.secs(W.state_pieces(s, "wake") + shift)
            kn, kw = kn[kn < len(lp)], kw[kw < len(lp)]
            lst.append(np.nanmean(lp[kn]) - np.nanmean(lp[kw]))
    pr("log delta power, nonREM packets minus WAKE, median over sessions:", fmt(np.median(on)), "; with the intervals shifted by 1800 s:",
       fmt(np.median(off)), f"; sessions {len(on)}, with a positive difference {int(np.sum(np.array(on) > 0))}")

Recordings deposited more than once, within and across the datasets.

In [3]:
# Recordings deposited more than once: sessions of the same rat and date, within each dataset, and the
# same session across the two datasets (identical spike trains, LFP length).
def same_trains(a, b):
    ka = {(len(x), round(float(x[0]), 5), round(float(x[-1]), 5)) for x in a["spikes"] if len(x)}
    return sum(1 for x in b["spikes"] if len(x) and (len(x), round(float(x[0]), 5), round(float(x[-1]), 5)) in ka)
def key(s):
    n = s["name"].replace("-", "_")
    return "_".join(n.split("_")[:2])
for ds in DS:
    ss = D[ds]
    for i in range(len(ss)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ss)):
            if key(ss[i]) == key(ss[j]):
                a, b = ss[i], ss[j]
                c = np.nan
                if "bp_delta" in a["G"] and "bp_delta" in b["G"] and a["G"]["T"] == b["G"]["T"]:
                    c = nancorr(np.log(a["G"]["bp_delta"]), np.log(b["G"]["bp_delta"]))
                pr(f"{ds}: {a['name']} and {b['name']}: identical spike trains {same_trains(a, b)} of {len(a['spikes'])}/{len(b['spikes'])}; "
                   f"LFP bytes {a.get('eeg_bytes')} / {b.get('eeg_bytes')}; good channels {a.get('goodeegchannel')} / {b.get('goodeegchannel')}; "
                   f"correlation of their delta power {fmt(c)}")
    pr(ds, "pairs of sessions with any identical spike train across different dates:",
       sum(1 for i in range(len(ss)) for j in range(i + 1, len(ss)) if key(ss[i]) != key(ss[j]) and same_trains(ss[i], ss[j]) > 0))
cr = {key(s) + ("_ACC" if s["name"].endswith("ACC") else ""): s for s in D["crcns-fcx-1"]}
rows = []
for s in D["000041"]:
    c = cr.get(key(s))
    if c is None:
        rows.append(f"{s['name']}: no CRCNS session"); continue
    st = same_trains(c, s)
    tt = [x for x in cr if x.startswith(key(s)) and x != key(s)]
    extra = "; " + ", ".join(f"{x}: {same_trains(cr[x], s)} identical" for x in tt) if tt else ""
    rows.append(f"{s['name']}: units {len(s['spikes'])} against {len(c['spikes'])} ({c['name']}), identical trains {st}, pE {len(s['E'])}/{len(c['E'])}, pI {len(s['I'])}/{len(c['I'])}{extra}")
pr("DANDI file against the CRCNS session of the same name:\n  " + "\n  ".join(rows))
pr("CRCNS sessions with no DANDI file:", sorted(set(cr) - {key(s) for s in D["000041"]}))

Data check, stated. The CRCNS files match the paper's description: 11 rats, 27 sessions, 1121 stable units (995 pE, 126 pI) of 1360 clustered, LFP at 1250 Hz, and, as printed below under the claims, Table S1's state durations, UP/DOWN counts and spindle values exactly. Each channel count found from a CRCNS .eeg stream equals its .xml. DANDI:000041 holds 22 of the 27 sessions: rat B22 (the three 2014052x sessions) and the ACC probes of Dino 061914 and 062014 are not in it, and Dino-061914 has no LFP. Its spike trains are those of CRCNS, train for train, except in Dino-072114 (13 of 16 identical), Dino-072314 and Dino-072414 (10 and 15 units more than CRCNS) and Dino-061814 (one more); in 7 sessions whose spike trains are all identical to CRCNS the pE and pI counts still differ (for example BWRat20-101513, 63 pE and 3 pI against 60 and 6), so its cell-type labels do not all follow _CellIDs. The Dino 061914 and 062014 ACC and mPFC folders of CRCNS hold LFP files of the same size with different good channels and no shared spike trains: two probes of one recording, counted as two sessions as Table S1 does. UP onsets are followed by a 50- to 70-fold rise of population spiking, which vanishes when the onsets are shifted by 1800 s, so spikes and the UP/DOWN intervals share a clock; state intervals and rates are consistent with that (WAKE and nonREM rates differ by state as below).

table1-dataset-counts¶

The data comprise 11 rats and 27 sessions, with 1360 clustered units of which 1121 are stable, 995 putative pyramidal cells (mean 36.9 per session, range 10 to 104) and 126 putative interneurons (4.67 per session, range 0 to 13).

Source: Results, Identification of brain states, sentence 1; Results, Assessment of firing patterns in different brain states, paragraph 1; Table S1, top. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

Result: reproduced. On CRCNS:fcx-1 every count matches: 11 rats, 27 sessions, 1121 stable units, 995 pE (36.85 per session, range 10 to 104), 126 pI (4.67, range 0 to 13), and 1360 clustered units in _SAll; the per-rat sessions and units equal Table S1. On DANDI:000041 there are 10 rats, 22 sessions, 945 units, 850 pE and 95 pI: rat B22 (3 sessions) and the two Dino ACC sessions are absent, so DANDI holds part of the data set.

wake-sleep-cycles¶

The data hold 54 WAKE-SLEEP episodes (WAKE of at least 7 min followed by SLEEP of at least 20 min), an average of 2.0 per session, and sessions without one were discarded.

Source: Results, Identification of brain states, paragraph 1; Results, Firing pattern and LFP changes across the course of sleep, sentence 1; Table S1. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [6]:
for ds in DS:
    ss = D[ds]
    n = [len(s["cycles"]) for s in ss]
    pr(f"== {ds} reading {'a (deposited WakeSleep intervals)' if ds=='crcns-fcx-1' else 'b (built from sleep_states)'}: "
       f"{sum(n)} cycles, {sum(n)/len(ss):.2f} per session, sessions without a cycle: {[s['name'] for s,k in zip(ss,n) if k==0]}")
    if ds == "crcns-fcx-1":
        nb = []
        for s in ss:
            I = s["ints"]
            ep = [("Non-REM", a, b) for a, b in I["SWSPacket"]] + [("REM", a, b) for a, b in I["REM"]]
            ep.sort(key=lambda e: e[1])
            seq, t = [], 0.0
            for l, a, b in ep:
                if a > t + 0.5:
                    seq.append(("Awake", t, a))
                seq.append((l, a, b)); t = b
            seq.append(("Awake", t, max(x.max() for x in s["spikes"] if len(x))))
            lab, a, b = zip(*seq)
            nb.append(len(W.derive_states(np.array(lab), np.array(a), np.array(b))["WakeSleep"]))
        pr(f"   reading b (built from the deposited packets and REM, all else awake): {sum(nb)} cycles, {sum(nb)/len(ss):.2f} per session, "
           f"sessions without: {sum(k==0 for k in nb)}")

== crcns-fcx-1 reading a (deposited WakeSleep intervals): 51 cycles, 1.89 per session, sessions without a cycle: []

Result: reproduced. CRCNS, reading a (deposited cycles): 51 cycles, 1.89 per session, every session has one; both within tolerance (54 +- 5.4, 2.0 +- 0.2). DANDI, reading b (cycles built from sleep_states): 47 cycles, 2.14 per session, and Dino-072114 has none. On CRCNS, cycles built by the same rules from the deposited packets and REM give 47, so the DANDI shortfall comes from rebuilding the intervals.

tables1-state-durations¶

Median durations are 1192 s for WAKE episodes, 2421 s for SLEEP episodes, 297 s for nonREM episodes, 98 s for REM episodes, and REM latency from SLEEP start is 647 s.

Source: Table S1, top. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [7]:
for ds in DS:
    ss = D[ds]
    wk = [c["wake"][1]-c["wake"][0] for s in ss for c in s["cycles"]]
    sl = [c["sleep"][1]-c["sleep"][0] for s in ss for c in s["cycles"]]
    ep = [e[1]-e[0] for s in ss for c in s["cycles"] for e in c["episodes"]]
    re_ = [e[1]-e[0] for s in ss for c in s["cycles"] for e in c["remep"]]
    re2 = [e[1]-e[0] for s in ss for c in s["cycles"] for e in c["rem"]]
    lat = [c["remep"][0][0]-c["sleep"][0] for s in ss for c in s["cycles"] if len(c["remep"])]
    lat2 = [c["rem"][0][0]-c["sleep"][0] for s in ss for c in s["cycles"] if len(c["rem"])]
    ws = [c["sleep"][1]-c["wake"][0] for s in ss for c in s["cycles"]]

ma-statistics¶

There are 790 microarousals, with median duration 15.9 s, 0.32 per minute, taking 9.1% of SLEEP time.

Source: Results, Identification of brain states, paragraph 2; Table S1. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [8]:
for ds in DS:
    ss = D[ds]
    allm, med_s, inc_s, pct_s = [], [], [], []
    for s in ss:
        d = [m[1]-m[0] for c in s["cycles"] for m in c["ma"]]
        slt = sum(c["sleep"][1]-c["sleep"][0] for c in s["cycles"])
        if slt == 0:
            continue
        allm += d
        if d: med_s.append(np.median(d))
        inc_s.append(len(d) / (slt / 60)); pct_s.append(100 * sum(d) / slt)
    pr(f"== {ds}: MAs in SLEEP of cycles {len(allm)}; median duration (a) all MAs {np.median(allm):.1f} s, (b) median of session medians "
       f"{np.median(med_s):.1f} s; incidence median over sessions {np.median(inc_s):.3f}/min (mean {np.mean(inc_s):.3f}); "
       f"percent of SLEEP median {np.median(pct_s):.1f}% (mean {np.mean(pct_s):.1f}%); sessions {len(inc_s)}")
    tot = sum(len(s["ints"]["MA"]) for s in ss)
    pr(f"   all MAs of the sessions, in or out of cycles: {tot}")

for ds in DS:
    ss = D[ds]
    allm = [m[1]-m[0] for s in ss for sl in np.asarray(s["ints"]["Sleep"]).reshape(-1, 2) for m in np.asarray(s["ints"]["MA"]).reshape(-1, 2) if m[0] >= sl[0] and m[1] <= sl[1]]
    pr(f"== {ds} (ma-statistics variant) MAs within any scored SLEEP: {len(allm)}, median {np.median(allm):.1f} s")

# Where the deposited MAs lie (verifier round 1, problem 4): per session, MAs inside the SLEEP of a
# WAKE-SLEEP cycle, inside another scored SLEEP, inside a scored WAKE, or in neither; and how many
# lie between two packets (a packet ending within 2 s before the MA and another starting within
# 2 s after it).
for ds in DS:
    pr(f"== {ds}: deposited MAs by where they lie (session: in cycle SLEEP / other SLEEP / WAKE / neither; between two packets)")
    tot = {"cycle SLEEP": [], "other SLEEP": [], "WAKE": [], "neither": []}; nbetween = 0
    for s in D[ds]:
        I = s["ints"]; M = np.asarray(I["MA"]).reshape(-1, 2)
        cs = np.array([c["sleep"] for c in s["cycles"]]).reshape(-1, 2)
        Sl = np.asarray(I["Sleep"]).reshape(-1, 2); Wk = np.asarray(I["Wake"]).reshape(-1, 2)
        pk = np.asarray(I["SWSPacket"]).reshape(-1, 2)
        def inside(m, X): return bool(((X[:, 0] <= m[0]) & (X[:, 1] >= m[1])).any()) if len(X) else False
        row = {k: 0 for k in tot}; nb_ = 0
        for m in M:
            k = "cycle SLEEP" if inside(m, cs) else "other SLEEP" if inside(m, Sl) else "WAKE" if inside(m, Wk) else "neither"
            row[k] += 1; tot[k].append(m[1] - m[0])
            if len(pk) and (np.abs(pk[:, 1] - m[0]) <= 2).any() and (np.abs(pk[:, 0] - m[1]) <= 2).any(): nb_ += 1
        nbetween += nb_
        pr(f"   {s['name']:18s} MAs {len(M):4d}: {row['cycle SLEEP']:3d} / {row['other SLEEP']:3d} / {row['WAKE']:4d} / {row['neither']:3d}; between packets {nb_:4d}; "
           f"packets {len(pk)}, cycles {len(s['cycles'])}")
    pr("   totals: " + "; ".join(f"{k} {len(v)} (median {np.median(v) if v else np.nan:.1f} s)" for k, v in tot.items()) + f"; between two packets {nbetween}")

ma-fraction-over-nrem-episodes¶

The fraction of time occupied by MAs decreases over the course of nonREM episodes (R = -0.85), with no statistical change over the course of SLEEP.

Source: Results, Identification of brain states, paragraph 2. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [9]:
def ma_frac(s, sub):
    k = W.secs(sub)
    if len(k) == 0: return None
    m = W.secs(np.concatenate([c["ma"] for c in s["cycles"]]) if s["cycles"] else np.zeros((0, 2)))
    return np.isin(k, m).mean()
for ds in DS:
    ss = D[ds]
    pr(f"== {ds} episodes:", rp(W.norm_corr(ss, "episode", ma_frac, readings=("c", "b"), normalize=False)))
    pr(f"   SLEEP (whole SLEEP time):", rp(W.norm_corr(ss, "sleep_all", ma_frac, readings=("c", "b"), normalize=False)))

fig2a-median-rates¶

Median firing rates of pE cells are 0.76 Hz in WAKE, 0.69 Hz in nonREM and 0.88 Hz in REM; of pI cells 5.59, 4.69 and 4.25 Hz.

Source: Results, Assessment of firing patterns in different brain states, paragraph 2; Figure 2A; Figure S2C. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [11]:
STATES = ["wake", "nrem", "rem"]
def rates_table(s, kind, reading):
    """Per-cell rates in each state: reading a, one row per cell and cycle; b, one row per cell over
    all its cycles; c, over the whole session's scored states."""
    cells = cells_of(s, kind)
    rows = []
    if reading == "a":
        for c in s["cycles"]:
            rows.append(np.stack([W.cell_rates(s, W.state_pieces(s, st, [c]), cells)[0] for st in STATES], 1))
    elif reading == "b":
        rows.append(np.stack([W.cell_rates(s, W.state_pieces(s, st), cells)[0] for st in STATES], 1))
    else:
        I = s["ints"]
        rows.append(np.stack([W.cell_rates(s, p, cells)[0] for p in [I["Wake"], I["SWSPacket"], I["REM"]]], 1))
    return np.concatenate(rows) if rows else np.zeros((0, 3))
RT = {}
for ds in DS:
    for kind in ["E", "I"]:
        for r in "abc":
            RT[ds, kind, r] = np.concatenate([rates_table(s, kind, r) for s in D[ds] if (s["cycles"] or r == "c")])
    for r in "abc":
        mE = np.nanmedian(RT[ds, "E", r], 0); mI = np.nanmedian(RT[ds, "I", r], 0)
        pr(f"== {ds} reading {r}: pE n={len(RT[ds,'E',r])} WAKE {mE[0]:.2f} nonREM {mE[1]:.2f} REM {mE[2]:.2f} Hz; "
           f"pI n={len(RT[ds,'I',r])} WAKE {mI[0]:.2f} nonREM {mI[1]:.2f} REM {mI[2]:.2f} Hz")
    rats = sorted(set(s["rat"] for s in D[ds]))
    byrat = []
    for rt in rats:
        X = [rates_table(s, "E", "b") for s in D[ds] if s["rat"] == rt and s["cycles"]]
        if X:
            m = np.nanmedian(np.concatenate(X), 0); byrat.append(f"{rt} {m[0]:.2f}/{m[1]:.2f}/{m[2]:.2f} (n={len(np.concatenate(X))})")
    pr(f"   by rat, pE medians WAKE/nonREM/REM, reading b: " + "; ".join(byrat))

fig2a-skewed-wide-distribution¶

The distribution of pE firing rates is strongly positively skewed, with a lognormal tail toward high rates and a supra-lognormal tail toward low rates, and spans three orders of magnitude, from 0.05 to 5 Hz.

Source: Results, Assessment of firing patterns in different brain states, paragraph 2; Figure 2A; Figure S2C. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [12]:
for ds in DS:
    for r in "ab":
        x = []
        for s in D[ds]:
            if not s["cycles"]: continue
            cyc = s["cycles"] if r == "b" else None
            groups = [[c] for c in s["cycles"]] if r == "a" else [s["cycles"]]
            for g in groups:
                p = np.concatenate([W.state_pieces(s, st, g) for st in STATES])
                x.append(W.cell_rates(s, p, s["E"])[0])
        x = np.concatenate(x); x = x[np.isfinite(x)]
        lx = np.log10(x[x > 0])
        pc = {q: np.percentile(x, q) for q in [1, 2.5, 5, 95, 97.5, 99]}
        pr(f"== {ds} reading {r} (all states pooled): n={len(x)}, skewness {stats.skew(x):.2f}, skewness of log10 rate {stats.skew(lx):.2f}, "
           f"5-95% {pc[5]:.3f}-{pc[95]:.2f} Hz, 1-99% {pc[1]:.3f}-{pc[99]:.2f}, 2.5-97.5% {pc[2.5]:.3f}-{pc[97.5]:.2f}, range {x.min():.4f}-{x.max():.1f}")
    for i, st in enumerate(STATES):
        x = RT[ds, "E", "b"][:, i]; x = x[np.isfinite(x)]
        pr(f"   state {st}: skew {stats.skew(x):.2f}, 5-95% {np.percentile(x,5):.3f}-{np.percentile(x,95):.2f}")

Rates over all states pooled are positively skewed (skewness 2.57 on CRCNS and 2.29 on DANDI, reading b), with a negative skewness of log10 rate (-1.10 and -1.31), a longer low tail than a lognormal. No percentile range matches 0.05 to 5 Hz within 10% at both ends: CRCNS 5-95% 0.070 to 3.26 Hz, 1-99% 0.013 to 5.69, 2.5-97.5% 0.032 to 4.17. The shape holds and the range does not.

burst-index-by-state¶

The burst index (fraction of spikes with ISIs below 15 ms) is highest in nonREM (median 11.8%), lowest in WAKE (4.0%), with REM (5.5%) slightly above WAKE.

Source: Results, Assessment of firing patterns in different brain states, paragraph 3. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [15]:
def burst_cell(s, pieces, cells, reading):
    """Burst index per cell over `pieces`, from spike times; an ISI counts only when both spikes lie
    in one interval of the state (round 1 also dropped every ISI that crossed a second of the grid)."""
    P = np.asarray(pieces, float).reshape(-1, 2)
    if reading == "a":
        n, sh = W.isi_counts(s, cells, P)
        return np.where(n > 0, sh / np.maximum(n, 1), np.nan)
    if reading == "b":
        bins = np.array([[t0, t0 + 10] for a, b in P for t0 in np.arange(np.ceil(a), np.floor(b) - 9, 10)]).reshape(-1, 2)
        if len(bins) == 0: return np.full(len(cells), np.nan)
        n, sh = W.isi_counts(s, cells, bins, per_piece=True)
        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
            return np.nanmean(np.where(n > 0, sh / np.maximum(n, 1), np.nan), 1)
    if len(P) == 0: return np.full(len(cells), np.nan)
    out = []
    for i in cells:
        t = s["sorted_spikes"][i]
        iv = np.searchsorted(P[:, 0], t, "right") - 1
        ok = (iv >= 0) & (t < P[np.maximum(iv, 0), 1]); t, iv = t[ok], iv[ok]
        if len(t) < 2: out.append(np.nan); continue
        sh = (np.diff(t) < 0.015) & (iv[1:] == iv[:-1])
        short = np.zeros(len(t), bool); short[1:] |= sh; short[:-1] |= sh
        out.append(short.mean())
    return np.array(out)
def burst_grid_round1(s, pieces, cells):
    """Round 1's reading a, for comparison: ISIs kept only when both spikes fall in the same second."""
    k = W.secs(pieces); out = []
    for i in cells:
        t = s["sorted_spikes"][i]; ki = t.astype(int)
        same = (ki[1:] == ki[:-1]) & np.isin(ki[1:], k)
        isi = np.diff(t)[same]
        out.append((isi <= 0.015).mean() if len(isi) else np.nan)
    return np.array(out)
BI = {}
for ds in DS:
    for r in "abc":
        X = []
        for s in D[ds]:
            if not s["cycles"]: continue
            X.append(np.stack([burst_cell(s, W.state_pieces(s, st), s["E"], r) for st in STATES], 1))
        X = np.concatenate(X) * 100; BI[ds, r] = X
        m = np.nanmedian(X, 0)
        cols = [X[np.isfinite(X[:, i]), i] for i in range(3)]
        kw = stats.kruskal(*cols)
        rs = stats.mannwhitneyu(cols[2], cols[0])
        allv = np.concatenate(cols); rk = stats.rankdata(allv); N = len(allv)
        n_ = [len(c) for c in cols]; mr = [rk[sum(n_[:i]):sum(n_[:i+1])].mean() for i in range(3)]
        z = (mr[2] - mr[0]) / np.sqrt(N * (N + 1) / 12 * (1 / n_[2] + 1 / n_[0])); pd = 2 * stats.norm.sf(abs(z))
        pr(f"== {ds} reading {r}: median burst index WAKE {m[0]:.1f}% nonREM {m[1]:.1f}% REM {m[2]:.1f}%; Kruskal-Wallis p={fmt(kw.pvalue)}; "
           f"REM vs WAKE rank-sum p={fmt(rs.pvalue)}, Dunn z={z:.2f} p={fmt(pd)}; cells with a value {n_}")
    X = np.concatenate([np.stack([burst_grid_round1(s, W.state_pieces(s, st), s["E"]) for st in STATES], 1) for s in D[ds] if s["cycles"]]) * 100
    m = np.nanmedian(X, 0)
    pr(f"   {ds} round 1 grid reading a (ISIs within one second only), for comparison: WAKE {m[0]:.1f}% nonREM {m[1]:.1f}% REM {m[2]:.1f}%")

On both datasets and every reading nonREM > REM > WAKE, the Kruskal-Wallis p is below 1e-37 and REM exceeds WAKE (CRCNS Dunn p = 1.3e-6, 7.7e-6 and 4.9e-6 under readings a, b and c). No reading puts the three medians within tolerance: CRCNS (a) 2.4/6.3/3.6%, (b) 2.2/6.0/3.0%, (c) 4.6/11.5/6.5% (WAKE/nonREM/REM, against 4.0/11.8/5.5); reading c has nonREM within tolerance and WAKE and REM above it. fig2c-acg-peaks¶

The average spike autocorrelogram of pE cells peaks near 8 ms in nonREM, with smaller peaks near 125 ms (theta) in REM and WAKE.

Source: Results, Assessment of firing patterns in different brain states, paragraph 3; Figure 2C and legend. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [16]:
MAXLAG = 0.5
def acg_cells(s, pieces, cells, maxlag=MAXLAG):
    """Autocorrelogram counts in 1 ms bins to maxlag, spike pairs within the same interval: bins
    [k, k+1) ms, and bins centred on whole ms, [k-0.5, k+0.5) (the convention of CCG-type code)."""
    pieces = np.asarray(pieces).reshape(-1, 2)
    nb = int(round(maxlag * 1000))
    out = np.zeros((len(cells), nb)); outc = np.zeros((len(cells), nb))
    if len(pieces) == 0:
        return out, outc
    for j, i in enumerate(cells):
        t = s["spikes"][i]
        iv = np.searchsorted(pieces[:, 0], t, "right") - 1
        ok = (iv >= 0) & (t < pieces[np.maximum(iv, 0), 1])
        t, iv = t[ok], iv[ok]
        for k in range(1, 400):
            if k >= len(t): break
            d = t[k:] - t[:-k]; same = iv[k:] == iv[:-k]
            m = same & (d < maxlag)
            if not m.any() and (d >= maxlag).all(): break
            np.add.at(out[j], np.minimum((d[m] * 1000).astype(int), nb - 1), 1)
            np.add.at(outc[j], np.minimum(np.rint(d[m] * 1000).astype(int), nb - 1), 1)
    return out, outc
ACG, ACGC = {}, {}
for ds in DS:
    for st in STATES:
        R_ = [acg_cells(s, W.state_pieces(s, st), s["E"]) for s in D[ds] if s["cycles"]]
        ACG[ds, st] = np.concatenate([a for a, _ in R_]); ACGC[ds, st] = np.concatenate([b for _, b in R_])
    for st in STATES:
        A = ACG[ds, st][:, :300]
        ok = A.max(1) > 0
        mean = (A[ok] / A[ok].max(1, keepdims=True)).mean(0)
        lag = np.arange(300) + 0.5
        pk = int(np.argmax(mean))
        loc = [i for i in range(60, 250) if mean[i] >= mean[i - 1] and mean[i] >= mean[i + 1]]
        loc_best = max(loc, key=lambda i: mean[i]) if loc else None
        sm = np.convolve(mean, np.ones(9) / 9, "same")
        loc_s = [i for i in range(60, 250) if sm[i] >= sm[i - 1] and sm[i] >= sm[i + 1]]
        lb = max(loc_s, key=lambda i: sm[i]) if loc_s else None
        pr(f"== {ds} {st}: cells {ok.sum()}, peak of mean ACG at {lag[pk]:.1f} ms; largest local max 60-250 ms at "
           f"{'none' if loc_best is None else lag[loc_best]} ms (9 ms smoothed: {'none' if lb is None else lag[lb]} ms, "
           f"height {sm[lb] if lb else np.nan:.3f} against {sm[60:250].min():.3f} minimum in the window)")
    for st in STATES:
        A = ACGC[ds, st][:, :300]; ok = A.max(1) > 0
        mean = (A[ok] / A[ok].max(1, keepdims=True)).mean(0); mean[0] = 0  # bin 0 holds only half a bin
        pk = int(np.argmax(mean))
        loc = [i for i in range(60, 250) if mean[i] >= mean[i - 1] and mean[i] >= mean[i + 1]]
        lb = max(loc, key=lambda i: mean[i]) if loc else None
        pr(f"   {ds} {st}, bins centred on whole ms: peak of mean ACG at {pk} ms (values at 7-11 ms: "
           f"{', '.join(f'{mean[i]:.3f}' for i in range(7, 12))}); largest local max 60-250 ms at {lb} ms")

The mean normalized autocorrelogram of pE cells in nonREM peaks in the bin [9, 10) ms on both datasets, whose centre, 9.5 ms, is outside 8 +- 0.8 ms; with bins centred on whole milliseconds the peak is at 10 ms on both. Only labelling the bin by its start (9 ms) puts it inside. The largest local maximum between 60 and 250 ms is at 113.5 ms in REM and 134.5 ms in WAKE on both, within 125 +- 12.5 ms; with bins centred on whole ms it is at 114 ms in REM and 99 ms in WAKE on CRCNS (113 and 99 ms on DANDI). Taking the bin centre, the theta part holds and the nonREM part does not.

fig2c-acg-decay¶

The autocorrelogram of pE cells decays faster in nonREM than in WAKE and REM (decay fit exponent medians -1.35, -0.83 and -0.80).

Source: Results, Assessment of firing patterns in different brain states, paragraph 3; Figure 2C. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [17]:
def decay(A, reading):
    out = []
    for a in A:
        if a.max() <= 0: out.append(np.nan); continue
        a = a / a.max(); pk = int(np.argmax(a))
        end = 100 if reading == "a" else 500
        lag = (np.arange(len(a)) + 0.5)
        sl = slice(pk, end)
        y, x = a[sl], lag[sl]; ok = y > 0
        if ok.sum() < 5: out.append(np.nan); continue
        if reading in ("a", "b"):
            out.append(np.polyfit(np.log(x[ok]), np.log(y[ok]), 1)[0])
        else:
            out.append(np.polyfit(x[ok] / 1000, np.log(y[ok]), 1)[0])
    return np.array(out)
for ds in DS:
    for r in "abc":
        ex = [decay(ACG[ds, st], r) for st in STATES]
        cols = [e[np.isfinite(e)] for e in ex]
        kw = stats.kruskal(*cols)
        pr(f"== {ds} reading {r}: median exponent WAKE {np.median(cols[0]):.2f} nonREM {np.median(cols[1]):.2f} REM {np.median(cols[2]):.2f} "
           f"(n {[len(c) for c in cols]}); Kruskal-Wallis p={fmt(kw.pvalue)}")

synchrony-skew¶

Population synchrony (fraction of pE cells firing in 50 ms windows) has a skewed distribution; more than 15% of pE cells rarely fire synchronously with others (in 4% of windows) while fewer than 4.2% fire synchronously in at least half of the windows.

Source: Results, Assessment of firing patterns in different brain states, paragraph 4; Figure S2F. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [18]:
def sync_session(s, pieces):
    E = s["E"]
    if len(E) < 2 or len(np.asarray(pieces).reshape(-1, 2)) == 0: return None
    k25 = []
    for a, b in np.asarray(pieces).reshape(-1, 2):
        k25.append(np.arange(int(np.ceil(a / 0.025)), int(b / 0.025) - 1))
    k25 = np.concatenate(k25)
    T = int(k25.max()) + 3
    act = np.zeros((len(E), T), bool)
    for j, i in enumerate(E):
        b = (s["spikes"][i] / 0.025).astype(int); act[j, b[b < T]] = True
    win = act[:, k25] | act[:, k25 + 1]  # 50 ms windows every 25 ms
    n = win.sum(0)
    fa = (win & (n >= 2)[None, :]).mean(1)  # fires with at least one other pE cell
    fb = win.mean(1)
    return fa, fb
for ds in DS:
    for nm, sel in [("all cycle time", None), ("wake", "wake"), ("nrem", "nrem"), ("rem", "rem")]:
        FA, FB = [], []
        for s in D[ds]:
            if not s["cycles"]: continue
            p = np.array([c["wake"][0:1].tolist() + [c["sleep"][1]] for c in s["cycles"]]) if sel is None else W.state_pieces(s, sel)
            r = sync_session(s, p)
            if r is None: continue
            FA.append(r[0]); FB.append(r[1])
        FA, FB = np.concatenate(FA), np.concatenate(FB)
        pr(f"== {ds} {nm}: n={len(FA)}; (a) with another pE cell: <=4% of windows {100*np.mean(FA<=0.04):.1f}%, >=50% {100*np.mean(FA>=0.5):.1f}%; "
           f"(b) any spike: <=4% {100*np.mean(FB<=0.04):.1f}%, >=50% {100*np.mean(FB>=0.5):.1f}%; skew (a) {stats.skew(FA):.2f}")

Over all cycle time, 62.9% (CRCNS) and 64.7% (DANDI) of pE cells fire with another pE cell in at most 4% of the 50 ms windows, and 0.0% in at least half; the per-cell measure is right-skewed (2.31 and 2.25). Both are beyond the paper's bounds in the stated direction, as the criterion asks, under readings a and b and in each state; the share of rarely synchronous cells is four times the paper's 15%, so the measure is unlikely to be the paper's (a question to a reader is filed).

fig1e-up-state-dynamics¶

Within UP states, firing rates of pyramidal cells and interneurons decrease over the course of the UP state, with decreasing E/(E+I) ratio and decreasing pE population synchrony; UP states begin with a surge of gamma power followed by increased sigma power.

Source: Results, Assessment of firing patterns in different brain states, paragraph 4; Figure 1E and legend; Figure S4C. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [20]:
NB = 10
def up_bins(s, ups):
    """Per UP state and normalized-time bin: pE rate, pI rate, fraction of pE and of pI cells spiking."""
    E, I = s["E"], s["I"]
    edges = ups[:, :1] + (ups[:, 1:] - ups[:, :1]) * np.linspace(0, 1, NB + 1)[None, :]
    dur = (ups[:, 1] - ups[:, 0]) / NB
    def cnts(cells):
        C = np.zeros((len(cells), len(ups), NB))
        for j, i in enumerate(cells):
            t = s["spikes"][i]
            for b in range(NB):
                C[j, :, b] = np.searchsorted(t, edges[:, b + 1]) - np.searchsorted(t, edges[:, b])
        return C
    CE = cnts(E); CI = cnts(I) if len(I) else None
    rE = CE.sum(0) / len(E) / dur[:, None]
    fE = (CE > 0).mean(0)
    rI = CI.sum(0) / len(I) / dur[:, None] if CI is not None else None
    fI = (CI > 0).mean(0) if CI is not None else None
    return rE, rI, fE, fI
for ds in DS:
    RE, RI, FE, EI = [], [], [], []
    for s in D[ds]:
        if not s["cycles"] or len(s["E"]) < 2: continue
        up = np.asarray(s.get("up", np.zeros((0, 2)))).reshape(-1, 2)
        sl = np.array([c["sleep"] for c in s["cycles"]])
        up = up[((up[:, 0][:, None] >= sl[:, 0]) & (up[:, 1][:, None] <= sl[:, 1])).any(1)]
        if len(up) == 0: continue
        rE, rI, fE, fI = up_bins(s, up)
        RE.append(rE); FE.append(fE)
        if rI is not None:
            RI.append(rI); EI.append(fE / np.where(fE + fI > 0, fE + fI, np.nan))
    out = {}
    for nm, X in [("pE rate", RE), ("pI rate", RI), ("pE synchrony", FE), ("E/(E+I)", EI)]:
        m = np.nanmean(np.concatenate(X), 0)
        R, p = stats.pearsonr(np.arange(NB), m)
        out[nm] = (R, p, m[0], m[-1])
        pr(f"== {ds} {nm}: R={R:.3f} p={fmt(p)}, first bin {m[0]:.3f}, last bin {m[-1]:.3f}, bins {np.round(m, 3).tolist()}")
    # UP-onset-triggered sigma and gamma power (short windows, 100 ms steps), UP states >= 1 s
    trig = {"sigma": [], "gamma": []}
    lags = np.arange(-5, 16)
    for s in D[ds]:
        if "short" not in s or not s["cycles"]: continue
        ts = s["short_t"]; pk = np.concatenate([c["packets"] for c in s["cycles"]])
        inn = np.zeros(len(ts), bool)
        for a, b in pk: inn |= (ts >= a) & (ts < b)
        up = np.asarray(s.get("up", np.zeros((0, 2)))).reshape(-1, 2)
        up = up[(up[:, 1] - up[:, 0]) >= 1.0]
        for band in trig:
            v = np.log(s["short"][band] + 1e-12); v = (v - v[inn].mean()) / v[inn].std()
            j = np.round((up[:, 0] - 0.1) / 0.1).astype(int)
            ok = (j + lags.min() >= 0) & (j + lags.max() < len(v))
            if ok.any(): trig[band].append(v[j[ok][:, None] + lags[None, :]])
    if trig["sigma"]:
        mg = np.concatenate(trig["gamma"]).mean(0); ms = np.concatenate(trig["sigma"]).mean(0)
        post = lags >= 0
        pg = lags[post][np.argmax(mg[post])] * 0.1; ps = lags[post][np.argmax(ms[post])] * 0.1
        pr(f"   UP-onset-triggered (UP >= 1 s, n={len(np.concatenate(trig['sigma']))}): gamma peak at {pg:.1f} s, sigma peak at {ps:.1f} s after onset; "
           f"gamma z {np.round(mg, 2).tolist()}; sigma z {np.round(ms, 2).tolist()} (lags -0.5 to 1.5 s)")

On CRCNS, across 10 bins of normalized UP time, the pI rate (R = -0.983), the pE rate (R = -0.293) and pE synchrony (R = -0.447) have negative R and are lower in the last bin than in the first; E/(E+I) has positive R (0.470). In the UP-onset-triggered power (UP states of at least 1 s), sigma peaks in the 0.0 s window and gamma in the 0.1 s window, so gamma does not precede sigma at this resolution. fig2de-fast-before-slow¶

In the early UP state pE cells fire in sequences stable across the first and second halves of SLEEP, and a cell's onset latency is negatively correlated with its firing rate.

Source: Results, Assessment of firing patterns in different brain states, paragraph 5; Figure 2D and 2E and legends. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [21]:
def first_latency(s, ups, cells, win=0.2):
    L = np.full((len(cells), len(ups)), np.nan)
    for j, i in enumerate(cells):
        t = s["spikes"][i]
        k = np.searchsorted(t, ups[:, 0])
        ok = k < len(t)
        lat = np.full(len(ups), np.nan); lat[ok] = t[k[ok]] - ups[ok, 0]
        lat[(lat > win) | (lat > (ups[:, 1] - ups[:, 0]))] = np.nan
        L[j] = lat
    return L
for ds in DS:
    for half in ["a", "b"]:
        X1, X2, RW, RN = [], [], [], []
        for s in D[ds]:
            if not s["cycles"] or len(s["E"]) < 3: continue
            up = np.asarray(s.get("up", np.zeros((0, 2)))).reshape(-1, 2)
            if len(up) < 20: continue
            if half == "a":
                m1 = np.zeros(len(up), bool); m2 = m1.copy()
                for c in s["cycles"]:
                    mid = (c["sleep"][0] + c["sleep"][1]) / 2
                    m1 |= (up[:, 0] >= c["sleep"][0]) & (up[:, 0] < mid); m2 |= (up[:, 0] >= mid) & (up[:, 0] < c["sleep"][1])
            else:
                mid = (up[0, 0] + up[-1, 1]) / 2; m1 = up[:, 0] < mid; m2 = ~m1
            L = first_latency(s, up, s["E"])
            X1.append(np.nanmean(L[:, m1], 1)); X2.append(np.nanmean(L[:, m2], 1))
            RW.append(W.wake_rate(s, s["E"])); RN.append(W.cell_rates(s, W.state_pieces(s, "nrem"), s["E"])[0])
        X1, X2, RW, RN = map(np.concatenate, (X1, X2, RW, RN))
        ok = np.isfinite(X1) & np.isfinite(X2)
        r12 = stats.pearsonr(X1[ok], X2[ok])
        lat = np.nanmean(np.c_[X1, X2], 1)
        res = []
        for nm, rr in [("WAKE", RW), ("nonREM", RN)]:
            k = np.isfinite(lat) & (rr > 0)
            res.append((nm, stats.pearsonr(np.log10(rr[k]), lat[k])))
        pr(f"== {ds} halves {half}: first vs second half latency R={r12[0]:.3f} p={fmt(r12[1])} n={ok.sum()}; latency vs log10 rate: "
           + "; ".join(f"{nm} R={r[0]:.3f} p={fmt(r[1])}" for nm, r in res))

fig2f-rate-group-correlations¶

In nonREM, pairwise spike-count correlations depend on firing rate group; pairs within the fastest group and within the slowest group are positively correlated, fast-firing pairs most highly, and fast and slow cells are negatively correlated with each other.

Source: Results, Assessment of firing patterns in different brain states, paragraph 5; Figure 2F and legend. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [22]:
def pair_corrs(s, cells, pieces, bin_=0.1):
    pieces = np.asarray(pieces).reshape(-1, 2)
    edges = np.concatenate([np.arange(a, b - bin_ / 2, bin_) for a, b in pieces]) if len(pieces) else np.zeros(0)
    if len(edges) < 10: return None
    C = np.zeros((len(cells), len(edges)))
    for j, i in enumerate(cells):
        t = s["spikes"][i]
        C[j] = np.searchsorted(t, edges + bin_) - np.searchsorted(t, edges)
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        R = np.corrcoef(C)
    return R
for ds in DS:
    for rd in ["wake sextiles", "nonREM-rate sextiles"]:
        if rd == "wake sextiles":
            W.sextiles(D[ds]); grp = [s["sextile"] for s in D[ds]]
        else:
            rn = [W.cell_rates(s, W.state_pieces(s, "nrem"), s["E"])[0] if s["cycles"] else np.full(len(s["E"]), np.nan) for s in D[ds]]
            flat = np.concatenate(rn); ok = np.isfinite(flat); rk = np.full(len(flat), -1)
            o = np.argsort(flat[ok], kind="stable"); q = np.zeros(ok.sum(), int); q[o] = (np.arange(ok.sum()) * 6) // ok.sum(); rk[ok] = q
            grp, i0 = [], 0
            for r in rn: grp.append(rk[i0:i0 + len(r)]); i0 += len(r)
        M = {(a, b): [] for a in range(6) for b in range(a, 6)}
        for s, g in zip(D[ds], grp):
            if not s["cycles"] or len(s["E"]) < 2: continue
            R = pair_corrs(s, s["E"], W.state_pieces(s, "nrem"))
            if R is None: continue
            n = len(s["E"])
            for i in range(n):
                for j in range(i + 1, n):
                    if g[i] < 0 or g[j] < 0 or not np.isfinite(R[i, j]): continue
                    a, b = sorted((g[i], g[j])); M[a, b].append(R[i, j])
        mean = {k: np.mean(v) if v else np.nan for k, v in M.items()}
        pv = {k: stats.wilcoxon(v).pvalue if len(v) > 5 else np.nan for k, v in M.items()}
        top = max(mean, key=lambda k: mean[k])
        pr(f"== {ds} {rd}: fastest-fastest {mean[5,5]:.4f} (p={fmt(pv[5,5])}, n={len(M[5,5])}), fastest-slowest {mean[0,5]:.4f} (p={fmt(pv[0,5])}, n={len(M[0,5])}), "
           f"slowest-slowest {mean[0,0]:.4f} (p={fmt(pv[0,0])}, n={len(M[0,0])}); largest mean at groups {top}")
        pr("   matrix (rows/cols lowest to highest):", np.array([[mean[tuple(sorted((a, b)))] for b in range(6)] for a in range(6)]).round(4).tolist())

post-sleep-wake-lower¶

pE rates in the 5 min of WAKE after SLEEP are lower than in the 5 min of WAKE before.

Source: Results, Firing pattern and LFP changes across the course of sleep, paragraph 1. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [25]:
def wake_windows(s, c, reading):
    """Last 5 min of the cycle's WAKE, and the first 5 min of WAKE after its SLEEP: (i) the next scored
    WAKE interval; (ii) the arousal of more than 120 s that ends the SLEEP."""
    pre = np.array([[max(c["wake"][0], c["wake"][1] - 300), c["wake"][1]]])
    Wk = np.asarray(s["ints"]["Wake"]).reshape(-1, 2)
    if reading == "i":
        nxt = Wk[Wk[:, 0] >= c["sleep"][1] - 2]
        if not len(nxt): return pre, None
        a = nxt[0, 0]
        return pre, np.array([[a, min(a + 300, nxt[0, 1])]])
    a = c["sleep"][1]
    # arousal after SLEEP: time until the next sleep state
    nxt_sleep = np.concatenate([np.asarray(s["ints"][k]).reshape(-1, 2) for k in ["SWSPacket", "REM"]])
    nxt_sleep = nxt_sleep[nxt_sleep[:, 0] > a + 1]
    end = nxt_sleep[:, 0].min() if len(nxt_sleep) else max(x.max() for x in s["spikes"] if len(x))
    if end - a <= 120: return pre, None
    return pre, np.array([[a, min(a + 300, end)]])
PW = {}
for ds in DS:
    for rr in ["i", "ii"]:
        for m1 in "ab":
            X, Y = [], []
            for s in D[ds]:
                xs, ys = [], []
                for c in s["cycles"]:
                    pre, post = wake_windows(s, c, rr)
                    if post is None: continue
                    xs.append(W.cell_rates(s, pre, s["E"])[0]); ys.append(W.cell_rates(s, post, s["E"])[0])
                if not xs: continue
                if m1 == "a": X += xs; Y += ys
                else: X.append(np.mean(xs, 0)); Y.append(np.mean(ys, 0))
            X, Y = np.concatenate(X), np.concatenate(Y)
            PW[ds, rr, m1] = (X, Y)
            pr(f"== {ds} WAKE-after {rr}, M1 {m1}: n={len(X)} pre mean {X.mean():.3f} median {np.median(X):.3f}, post mean {Y.mean():.3f} median {np.median(Y):.3f} Hz; "
               f"signed-rank p two {fmt(stats.wilcoxon(X, Y).pvalue)} one {fmt(stats.wilcoxon(X, Y, alternative='greater').pvalue)}; "
               f"rank-sum two {fmt(stats.mannwhitneyu(X, Y).pvalue)} one {fmt(stats.mannwhitneyu(X, Y, alternative='greater').pvalue)}")

Result: reproduced. CRCNS, with the arousal that ends SLEEP as the WAKE after (reading ii), pE rates fall from 1.261 to 1.135 Hz (signed-rank p = 3.1e-11 by cell and cycle; 1.7e-6 two-sided, 8.3e-7 one-sided by cell), below the 1e-6 bound by cell and cycle; with the next scored WAKE (reading i) p = 0.018. DANDI: the decrease holds under every reading with two-sided signed-rank p between 2.4e-5 and 1.1e-3, not below 1e-6. Rank-sum tests are weaker: the one-sided rank-sum p is 0.027 on CRCNS under reading ii with one entry per cell and cycle, and 0.055 to 0.51 under the other readings on both datasets.

def cv_fn(s, sub):
    if len(s["E"]) < 3: return None
    r, n = W.cell_rates(s, sub, s["E"])
    if n == 0 or np.nanmean(r) == 0: return None
    return np.nanstd(r) / np.nanmean(r)

fig3c-spindles-over-sleep¶

Over SLEEP spindle incidence (1.94/min) decreases while spindle duration (0.52 s), frequency (13.93 Hz) and amplitude (203.3 uV) do not change.

Source: Results, Firing pattern and LFP changes across the course of sleep, paragraph 3; Figure 3C, bottom; Table S1. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [29]:
def gratio(num, den=None, per_min=False):
    def f(s, sub):
        if num not in s["G"]: return None
        a, n = W.gsum(s, num, sub)
        if den is None:
            return a / n * (60 if per_min else 1) if n else None
        b, _ = W.gsum(s, den, sub)
        return a / b if b > 0 else None
    return f
for ds in DS:
    ss = [s for s in D[ds] if s["cycles"] and "sp_n" in s["G"]]
    sp_n = sum(W.gsum(s, "sp_n", W.state_pieces(s, "nrem"))[0] for s in ss)
    t_n = sum(W.gsum(s, "sp_n", W.state_pieces(s, "nrem"))[1] for s in ss)
    inc_s = [W.gsum(s, "sp_n", W.state_pieces(s, "nrem"))[0] / W.gsum(s, "sp_n", W.state_pieces(s, "nrem"))[1] * 60 for s in ss]
    sp = [s["spindles"] for s in ss]
    allsp = {k: np.concatenate([x[k] for x in sp]) for k in ["dur", "freq", "amp_uV"]}
    pr(f"== {ds} ({'deposited _Spindles, reading a' if ds!='000041' else 'detected here, reading b'}): {sum(len(x['start']) for x in sp)} spindles in the sessions, "
       f"{sp_n:.0f} in nonREM of cycles; incidence {sp_n/t_n*60:.2f}/min pooled, median over sessions {np.median(inc_s):.2f}/min; "
       f"median duration {np.nanmedian(allsp['dur']):.3f} s, frequency {np.nanmedian(allsp['freq']):.2f} Hz, amplitude {np.nanmedian(allsp['amp_uV']):.1f} uV; "

fig3f-within-up-changes¶

Within UP states, pE rates decrease over SLEEP, and from first to last packet the fastest sextile and interneurons decrease while the slowest sextile increases.

Source: Results, Firing pattern and LFP changes across the course of sleep, paragraph 3; Figure 3F and legend; Figure S3C. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [31]:
def up_rate(cells_fn):
    def f(s, sub):
        if "upcnt" not in s["G"]: return None
        cells = cells_fn(s)
        if len(cells) == 0: return None
        a, n = W.gsum(s, "upcnt", sub); t, _ = W.gsum(s, "up_occ", sub)
        return a[cells].sum() / len(cells) / t if t > 0 else None
    return f
for ds in DS:
    ss = [s for s in D[ds] if s["cycles"] and len(s.get("up", []))]
    pr(f"== {ds} within-UP pE rate over SLEEP:", rp(W.norm_corr(ss, "sleep", up_rate(lambda s: s["E"]))))
    out = {}
    for nm, sel in [("top sextile", lambda s: s["E"][s["sextile"] == 5]), ("bottom sextile", lambda s: s["E"][s["sextile"] == 0]), ("pI", lambda s: s["I"])]:
        ch = []
        for s in ss:
            cells = sel(s)
            if len(cells) == 0: continue
            for c in s["cycles"]:
                if len(c["packets"]) < 2: continue
                r = []
                for p in (c["packets"][:1], c["packets"][-1:]):
                    a, n = W.gsum(s, "upcnt", p); t, _ = W.gsum(s, "up_occ", p)
                    r.append(a[cells] / t if t > 0 else np.full(len(cells), np.nan))
                ch.append(r[1] - r[0])
        ch = np.concatenate(ch); ch = ch[np.isfinite(ch)]
        pr(f"   {nm}: last minus first packet within-UP rate, mean {ch.mean():.3f} Hz, median {np.median(ch):.3f}, n={len(ch)}, signed-rank p={fmt(stats.wilcoxon(ch).pvalue)}")

def fig3e_tests(ds, rr, m1, key):
    X, Y = PW[ds, rr, m1]
    sx = []
    for s in D[ds]:
        nv = sum(1 for c in s["cycles"] if wake_windows(s, c, rr)[1] is not None)
        if nv == 0: continue
        sx.append(np.tile(s[key], nv) if m1 == "a" else s[key])
    sx = np.concatenate(sx); out = []
    for q in range(6):
        m = sx == q; d = Y[m] - X[m]
        alt = "less" if q >= 3 else "greater"
        p = stats.wilcoxon(Y[m], X[m], alternative=alt).pvalue if (d != 0).sum() > 5 else np.nan
        out.append(f"S{q+1}: mean change {d.mean():+.3f} Hz, one-sided ({'decrease' if q>=3 else 'increase'}) p={fmt(p)}, n={m.sum()}")
    return "; ".join(out)
def test_windows(rr):
    def f(s):
        w = [x for c in s["cycles"] for x in wake_windows(s, c, rr) if x is not None]
        return np.concatenate(w) if w else np.zeros((0, 2))
    return f
for ds in DS:
    for rr in ["i", "ii"]:
        for m1 in "ab":
            pr(f"== {ds} WAKE-after {rr} (M1 {m1}, sextile 1 lowest): " + fig3e_tests(ds, rr, m1, "sextile"))
        # held-out variant: cells ranked on WAKE without the two windows the test compares
        W.sextiles(D[ds], exclude=test_windows(rr), key="sext_ho")
        for m1 in "ab":
            pr(f"   variant, sextiles ranked on WAKE without the test windows (M1 {m1}): " + fig3e_tests(ds, rr, m1, "sext_ho"))

With sextiles ranked on WAKE without the two test windows the same four hold (p = 7.2e-12, 1.0e-5, 0.021, 0.011), so the result does not come from ranking on the windows tested. With one entry per cell (M1 b) the fourth sextile misses (p = 0.077). With the next scored WAKE (reading i) the fourth sextile fails. DANDI, reading ii, M1 a: all four hold (1.1e-5, 0.017, 0.017; 0.019).

Band powers z-scored per session, used by the LFP claims.

In [34]:
# Band powers z-scored per session ([claim] fig4i, "z-scored per session (a standard choice)"): log
# power, mean and SD over the nonREM packets of the session's cycles.
for ds in DS:
    for s in D[ds]:
        G = s["G"]
        if "bp_delta" not in G or not s["cycles"]: continue
        k = W.secs(W.state_pieces(s, "nrem")); k = k[k < G["T"]]
        for b in ["delta", "delta14", "sigma", "gamma", "theta", "broad"]:
            v = np.log(G["bp_" + b]); m = np.nanmean(v[k]); sd = np.nanstd(v[k])
            G["bpz_" + b] = (v - m) / sd
            G["bpn_" + b] = G["bp_" + b] / np.nanmean(G["bp_" + b][k])
        if "bt_theta" in G:
            G["thetaratio"] = G["bt_theta"] / G["bt_broad"]
        else:
            G["thetaratio"] = G["bp_theta"] / G["bp_broad"]
        v = np.log(G["bp_theta"]); G["thetaz"] = (v - np.nanmean(v[k])) / np.nanstd(v[k])
    pr(ds, "sessions with band power:", sum("bpz_delta" in s["G"] for s in D[ds]), "of", len(D[ds]))

fig4-late-packet-sigma-delta¶

In the final portion of nonREM packets, the positive correlation between delta and sigma power gives way to a sudden increase of sigma power with a concurrent decrease of delta power.

Source: Results, Firing rate and LFP changes within nonREM episodes and packets, paragraph 3; Figure 4A-B i. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [37]:
for ds in DS:
    for rd in ["a", "b"]:
        ds_, dd_, cf, cr = [], [], [], []
        for s in D[ds]:
            if "bpz_sigma" not in s["G"]: continue
            G = s["G"]
            for p in W.state_pieces(s, "nrem"):
                a, b = int(np.ceil(p[0])), int(np.floor(p[1]))
                L = 20 if rd == "a" else max(2, (b - a) // 10)
                if b - a < 2 * L + 2: continue
                fin = np.arange(b - L, b); pre = np.arange(b - 2 * L, b - L); rest = np.arange(a, b - L)
                sg, dl = G["bpz_sigma"], G["bpz_delta"]
                ds_.append(np.nanmean(sg[fin]) - np.nanmean(sg[pre])); dd_.append(np.nanmean(dl[fin]) - np.nanmean(dl[pre]))
                if L >= 5 and len(rest) >= 5:
                    cf.append(nancorr(sg[fin], dl[fin])); cr.append(nancorr(sg[rest], dl[rest]))
        ds_, dd_ = np.array(ds_), np.array(dd_)
        cf, cr = np.array(cf), np.array(cr); ok = np.isfinite(cf) & np.isfinite(cr)
        pr(f"== {ds} reading {rd}: packets {len(ds_)}; sigma final minus preceding {np.nanmean(ds_):+.3f} SD (signed-rank p={fmt(stats.wilcoxon(ds_).pvalue)}), "
           f"delta {np.nanmean(dd_):+.3f} SD (p={fmt(stats.wilcoxon(dd_).pvalue)}); delta-sigma correlation in the rest {np.mean(cr[ok]):.3f}, in the final portion "
           f"{np.mean(cf[ok]):.3f} (n={ok.sum()}, signed-rank p={fmt(stats.wilcoxon(cf[ok], cr[ok]).pvalue)})")

fig4-updown-within-packets¶

Within packets UP and DOWN incidence increase, UP duration decreases and DOWN duration increases, so the UP/DOWN ratio falls.

Source: Results, Firing rate and LFP changes within nonREM episodes and packets, paragraph 2; Figure 4A-B ii. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [38]:
def ud_ratio_a(s, sub):
    a, n = W.gsum(s, "up_dur", sub); b, m = W.gsum(s, "dn_dur", sub)
    nu, _ = W.gsum(s, "up_n", sub); nd, _ = W.gsum(s, "dn_n", sub)
    return (a / nu) / (b / nd) if nu > 0 and nd > 0 and b > 0 else None
def ud_ratio_b(s, sub):
    a, _ = W.gsum(s, "up_occ", sub); b, _ = W.gsum(s, "dn_occ", sub)
    return a / b if b > 0 else None
for ds in DS:
    ss = [s for s in D[ds] if s["cycles"] and len(s.get("up", []))]
    for nm, fn in UDF + [("UP/DOWN ratio a (durations)", ud_ratio_a), ("UP/DOWN ratio b (time)", ud_ratio_b)]:
        pr(f"== {ds} {nm} over packets:", rp(W.norm_corr(ss, "packet", fn, readings=("b", "c"))))

fig4e-late-packet-sigma¶

UP states late in nonREM packets have more sigma power than UP states early in packets.

Source: Results, Firing rate and LFP changes within nonREM episodes and packets, paragraphs 3 and 6; Figure 4E; Figure S4B and S4D and legends. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [40]:
def up_sigma(s, up, reading):
    ts = s["short_t"]; v = np.log(s["short"]["sigma"] + 1e-12)
    k = W.secs(W.state_pieces(s, "nrem")); inn = np.isin(ts.astype(int), k)
    v = (v - v[inn].mean()) / v[inn].std()
    out = []
    for a, b in up:
        if reading == "a":
            m = (ts >= a) & (ts < b)
        else:
            m = (ts >= a) & (ts < a + 1.0)
        out.append(v[m].mean() if m.any() else np.nan)
    return np.array(out)
for ds in DS:
    for rd in ["a", "b"]:
        E_, L_ = [], []
        for s in D[ds]:
            if "short" not in s or not s["cycles"]: continue
            up = np.asarray(s.get("up", np.zeros((0, 2)))).reshape(-1, 2)
            up = up[(up[:, 1] - up[:, 0]) > (0.5 if rd == "a" else 0.999)]
            for p in W.state_pieces(s, "nrem"):
                L = (p[1] - p[0]) / 3
                e = up[(up[:, 0] >= p[0]) & (up[:, 1] <= p[0] + L)]; l = up[(up[:, 0] >= p[1] - L) & (up[:, 1] <= p[1])]
                if len(e): E_.append(up_sigma(s, e, rd))
                if len(l): L_.append(up_sigma(s, l, rd))
        E_, L_ = np.concatenate(E_), np.concatenate(L_)
        E_, L_ = E_[np.isfinite(E_)], L_[np.isfinite(L_)]
        r = stats.mannwhitneyu(L_, E_)
        pr(f"== {ds} reading {rd}: UP-state sigma (z) first third {np.mean(E_):.3f} (n={len(E_)}), last third {np.mean(L_):.3f} (n={len(L_)}); rank-sum p={fmt(r.pvalue)}")
# S4B per-pixel map, coarse: UP states over 500 ms, 5 bins of normalized UP time x the two short-window
# bands (z-scored log power over nonREM); Welch t-test of last-third against first-third UP states
# per pixel. The 200 ms windows give 5 Hz resolution, so the map has two bands, not a spectrum.
def up_map(s, up, nb=5):
    ts = s["short_t"]; k = W.secs(W.state_pieces(s, "nrem")); inn = np.isin(ts.astype(int), k)
    Z = []
    for b_ in ["sigma", "gamma"]:
        v = np.log(s["short"][b_] + 1e-12); Z.append((v - v[inn].mean()) / v[inn].std())
    out = np.full((len(up), 2, nb), np.nan)
    i0 = np.searchsorted(ts, up[:, 0]); i1 = np.searchsorted(ts, up[:, 1])
    for u, (a, b) in enumerate(up):
        idx = np.arange(i0[u], i1[u])
        if len(idx) == 0: continue
        bi = np.minimum(((ts[idx] - a) / (b - a) * nb).astype(int), nb - 1)
        for j in range(2):
            out[u, j] = [Z[j][idx[bi == q]].mean() if (bi == q).any() else np.nan for q in range(nb)]
    return out
for ds in DS:
    E_, L_ = [], []
    for s in D[ds]:
        if "short" not in s or not s["cycles"]: continue
        up = np.asarray(s.get("up", np.zeros((0, 2)))).reshape(-1, 2); up = up[(up[:, 1] - up[:, 0]) > 0.5]
        for p in W.state_pieces(s, "nrem"):
            L = (p[1] - p[0]) / 3
            e = up[(up[:, 0] >= p[0]) & (up[:, 1] <= p[0] + L)]; l = up[(up[:, 0] >= p[1] - L) & (up[:, 1] <= p[1])]
            if len(e): E_.append(up_map(s, e))
            if len(l): L_.append(up_map(s, l))
    E_, L_ = np.concatenate(E_), np.concatenate(L_)
    for j, b_ in enumerate(["sigma 9-25 Hz", "gamma 40-100 Hz"]):
        cells_ = []
        for q in range(5):
            x, y = L_[:, j, q], E_[:, j, q]; x, y = x[np.isfinite(x)], y[np.isfinite(y)]
            t = stats.ttest_ind(x, y, equal_var=False)
            cells_.append(f"t={t.statistic:.1f} p={fmt(t.pvalue)}")
        pr(f"== {ds} S4B map, {b_}, late minus early by fifth of UP time: " + " | ".join(cells_))

def burst_a(s, sub):
    if len(s["E"]) == 0: return None
    n, sh = W.isi_counts(s, s["E"], sub)
    v = sh[n > 0] / n[n > 0]
    return v.mean() if len(v) else None
def burst_pooled(s, sub):
    n, sh = W.isi_counts(s, s["E"], sub)
    return sh.sum() / n.sum() if n.sum() > 0 else None

for ds in DS:
    rows = []
    for s in D[ds]:
        if not s["cycles"] or "bpz_delta" not in s["G"] or not len(s.get("up", [])): continue
        recs = []
        for c in s["cycles"]:
            pk = c["packets"]
            if len(pk) == 0: continue
            rt = {q: np.array([np.nanmean(W.cell_rates(s, [p], s["E"][s["sextile"] == q])[0]) if (s["sextile"] == q).any() else np.nan for p in pk]) for q in (0, 5)}
            for q in rt: rt[q] = rt[q] / np.nanmean(rt[q]) if np.nanmean(rt[q]) > 0 else rt[q] * np.nan
            for j, p in enumerate(pk):
                nu, n = W.gsum(s, "up_n", [p]); nd, _ = W.gsum(s, "dn_n", [p])
                du, _ = W.gsum(s, "up_dur", [p]); dd, _ = W.gsum(s, "dn_dur", [p])
                last = [[max(p[0], p[1] - 20), p[1]]]
                recs.append([rt[5][j], rt[0][j], W.gmean(s, "bpz_delta", [p]), dd / nd if nd else np.nan, nd / n * 60 if n else np.nan,
                             du / nu if nu else np.nan, W.gmean(s, "bpz_gamma", [p]), W.gmean(s, "bpz_sigma", last)])
        recs = np.array(recs)
        for col in [3, 4, 5]:  # z-score the per-packet slow-wave metrics within session
            v = recs[:, col]; recs[:, col] = (v - np.nanmean(v)) / np.nanstd(v)
        rows.append(recs)
    R = np.concatenate(rows)
    names = ["delta power", "DOWN duration", "DOWN incidence", "UP duration", "gamma power", "sigma last 20 s"]
    out = []
    for gi, g in [(0, "top"), (1, "bottom")]:
        for j, nm in enumerate(names):
            x, y = R[:, gi], R[:, 2 + j]; ok = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
            r = stats.pearsonr(x[ok], y[ok]); out.append(f"{g}~{nm}: R={r[0]:.3f} p={fmt(r[1])} n={ok.sum()}")
    pr(f"== {ds} ({len(rows)} sessions): " + "; ".join(out))

Result: not reproduced. On CRCNS all six correlations have the paper's sign at p < 0.05, but only DOWN duration (R = -0.365, p = 4.5e-19), DOWN incidence (-0.316, 1.5e-14) and UP duration (0.203, 1.3e-6) meet their bounds; delta (R = -0.144, p = 6e-4 against 1e-10), gamma (0.257, 5.7e-10 against 1e-10) and bottom-sextile late sigma (0.183, 5.6e-6 against 1e-10) do not. A correlation holds when it meets M4's reproduced level (sign and bound), so three of six hold, fewer than the four needed for partial. The four absences hold. Counting a correlation at p < 0.05 as holding, all six would hold and the claim would be reproduced.

DANDI: pI and the slowest sextile rise under every reading, as on CRCNS; the top sextile falls under reading b (2.789 to 2.719 Hz, p = 0.0051) and under a(ii) (p = 0.051), and rises slightly under a(i) (2.789 to 2.808 Hz, p = 0.64).

figs5-within-wake-rem¶

Within WAKE the two highest sextiles increase and the two lowest decrease their rates, opposite to nonREM; within REM all sextiles except the fourth increase.

Source: Results, Firing rate and LFP changes within nonREM episodes and packets, last paragraph; Figure S5A and S5B and legend. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [46]:
def sext_rate_exact(q, key="sextile"):
    def f(s, sub):
        cells = s["E"][s[key] == q]
        if len(cells) == 0: return None
        r = W.exact_rates(s, sub, cells)
        return np.nanmean(r) if np.isfinite(r).any() else None
    return f
def wake_entry(ds, ss, key):
    out = []
    for q in range(5, -1, -1):
        d = []
        for s in ss:
            cells = s["E"][s[key] == q]
            if len(cells) == 0: continue
            for c in s["cycles"]:
                a, b = c["wake"]; L = b - a
                pre = [[max(0, a - 0.25 * L), a]]; first = [[a, a + 0.1 * L]]
                d.append(W.cell_rates(s, first, cells)[0] - W.cell_rates(s, pre, cells)[0])
        d = np.concatenate(d); d = d[np.isfinite(d)]
        out.append(f"{6-q}: mean {d.mean():+.3f} Hz, p={fmt(stats.wilcoxon(d).pvalue)} n={len(d)}")
    return "; ".join(out)
for ds in DS:
    ss = [s for s in D[ds] if s["cycles"]]
    rem, remx, wk = [], [], []
    for q in range(5, -1, -1):  # S5 numbering, 1 = highest
        rem.append(W.norm_corr(ss, "rem", sext_rate(q), readings=("c",))["c"])
        remx.append(W.norm_corr(ss, "rem", sext_rate_exact(q), readings=("c",))["c"])
        wk.append(W.norm_corr(ss, "wake", sext_rate(q), readings=("c",))["c"])
    pr(f"== {ds} REM (50 bins, exact spike times), S5 sextiles 1..6: " + "; ".join(f"{i+1}: R={r[0]:.3f} p={fmt(r[1])} n={r[2]}" for i, r in enumerate(remx)))
    pr(f"   REM (50 bins, 1 s grid, seconds centred in the bin): " + "; ".join(f"{i+1}: R={r[0]:.3f} p={fmt(r[1])} n={r[2]}" for i, r in enumerate(rem)))
    pr(f"   WAKE (a, 50 bins): " + "; ".join(f"{i+1}: R={r[0]:.3f} p={fmt(r[1])}" for i, r in enumerate(wk)))
    pr(f"   WAKE (b, first tenth minus the quarter-length before): " + wake_entry(ds, ss, "sextile"))
    # held-out variant: cells ranked on WAKE without the first tenth of each cycle's WAKE and the period before it
    def excl(s):
        w = [[max(0, c["wake"][0] - 0.25 * (c["wake"][1] - c["wake"][0])), c["wake"][0] + 0.1 * (c["wake"][1] - c["wake"][0])] for c in s["cycles"]]
        return np.array(w).reshape(-1, 2)
    W.sextiles(D[ds], exclude=excl, key="sext_ho")
    pr(f"   WAKE (b), variant with sextiles ranked on WAKE without the test windows: " + wake_entry(ds, ss, "sext_ho"))

Triplets of sub-states (M6 of the claims file), used by the Figure 5 claims.

In [47]:
# [claim] M6; [paper] Supplemental Experimental Procedures, Spiking metrics: triplets of nonREM packets,
# REM episodes, MAs and WAKE; nonREM-REM-nonREM triplets kept unless a WAKE (> 120 s) follows the REM
# before the second packet. Sequences are built within each SLEEP of a cycle from the packets (N),
# MAs (M), REM (R) and WAKE interruptions of 40-120 s (W).
def sequence(c):
    ev = [("N", p) for p in c["packets"]] + [("M", m) for m in c["ma"]] + [("R", r) for r in c["rem"]] + [("W", w) for w in c["wi"]]
    ev.sort(key=lambda e: e[1][0])
    return ev
def triplets(s, kind, wake_reading="b"):
    out = []
    for ci, c in enumerate(s["cycles"]):
        ev = sequence(c)
        L = [e[0] for e in ev]
        if kind == "MNM":
            for i in range(len(ev) - 2):
                if L[i:i + 3] == ["M", "N", "M"]: out.append((ev[i][1], ev[i + 1][1], ev[i + 2][1]))
        elif kind == "RNR":
            idx = [i for i, l in enumerate(L) if l == "R"]
            for a, b in zip(idx[:-1], idx[1:]):
                mid = L[a + 1:b]
                if mid and all(x in "NM" for x in mid) and "N" in mid:
                    nn = [ev[k][1] for k in range(a + 1, b) if L[k] == "N"]
                    out.append((ev[a][1], np.array([nn[0][0], nn[-1][1]]), ev[b][1]))
        elif kind in ("NMN", "NWN"):
            for i in range(len(ev) - 2):
                if L[i:i + 3] == ["N", kind[1], "N"]: out.append((ev[i][1], ev[i + 1][1], ev[i + 2][1]))
        elif kind == "NRN":
            for i in range(len(ev)):
                if L[i] != "N": continue
                j = i + 1
                if j < len(L) and L[j] == "R":
                    k = j + 1
                    while k < len(L) and L[k] in "MWR": k += 1
                    if k < len(L) and L[k] == "N":
                        r = [ev[q][1] for q in range(j, k) if L[q] == "R"]
                        out.append((ev[i][1], np.array([r[0][0], r[-1][1]]), ev[k][1]))
    if kind == "NWN" and wake_reading == "a":
        out = []
        for c0, c1 in zip(s["cycles"][:-1], s["cycles"][1:]):
            if len(c0["packets"]) and len(c1["packets"]):
                out.append((c0["packets"][-1], c1["wake"], c1["packets"][0]))
    return out
def triplet_changes(ds, kind, **kw):
    """Per (cell, triplet): sextile, rate n, rate n+1, WAKE rate, session, triplet index."""
    rows = []
    for si, s in enumerate(D[ds]):
        for ti, (a, b, c) in enumerate(triplets(s, kind, **kw)):
            r0 = W.cell_rates(s, [a], s["E"])[0]; r1 = W.cell_rates(s, [c], s["E"])[0]
            for j in range(len(s["E"])):
                rows.append([s["sextile"][j], r0[j], r1[j], s["wake_rate_E"][j], si, ti, j])
    return np.array(rows).reshape(-1, 7)
def sextile_tests(X, label):
    out = []
    for q in range(5, -1, -1):
        m = X[:, 0] == q; d = X[m, 2] - X[m, 1]
        # M1 b: one value per cell, its changes averaged over triplets
        keys = X[m][:, [4, 6]]
        if len(d) < 3: out.append(f"S{q+1}: n={len(d)}"); continue
        _, inv = np.unique(keys, axis=0, return_inverse=True)
        db = np.bincount(inv.ravel(), d) / np.bincount(inv.ravel())
        out.append(f"S{q+1} (1 lowest): mean {d.mean():+.3f} Hz n={len(d)} signed-rank p={fmt(stats.wilcoxon(d).pvalue)} t p={fmt(stats.ttest_1samp(d, 0).pvalue)}; "
                   f"per cell n={len(db)} mean {db.mean():+.3f} p={fmt(stats.wilcoxon(db).pvalue)}")
    pr(f"   {label}:\n     " + "\n     ".join(out))
def s5_corr(X):
    ok = (X[:, 1] > 0) & (X[:, 2] > 0) & (X[:, 3] > 0)
    Y = X[ok]; d = np.log10(Y[:, 2]) - np.log10(Y[:, 1])
    _, inv = np.unique(Y[:, [4, 6]], axis=0, return_inverse=True); inv = inv.ravel()
    db = np.bincount(inv, d) / np.bincount(inv); wr = np.bincount(inv, Y[:, 3]) / np.bincount(inv)
    ra = stats.pearsonr(np.log10(wr), db); rb = stats.pearsonr(wr, db)
    return f"log change vs log10 WAKE rate R={ra[0]:.3f} p={fmt(ra[1])}; vs linear WAKE rate R={rb[0]:.3f} p={fmt(rb[1])}; cells {len(db)} (dropped {int((~ok).sum())} cell-triplets with a zero rate)"
TR = {}
for ds in DS:
    for kind in ["MNM", "RNR", "NMN", "NRN"]:
        TR[ds, kind] = triplet_changes(ds, kind)
    for wr in "ab":
        TR[ds, "NWN" + wr] = triplet_changes(ds, "NWN", wake_reading=wr)
    pr(ds, "triplets:", {k: int(sum(len(triplets(s, k)) for s in D[ds])) for k in ["MNM", "RNR", "NMN", "NRN"]},
       "NWN (a scored WAKE):", sum(len(triplets(s, "NWN", "a")) for s in D[ds]), "NWN (b arousal 40-120 s):", sum(len(triplets(s, "NWN", "b")) for s in D[ds]))

for ds in DS:

Result: reproduced. Reading a (a scored WAKE between the last packet of one SLEEP and the first of the next): 24 triplets on CRCNS, within 24 +- 2.4. The top sextile increases (+0.149 Hz, signed-rank p = 0.017), the lowest does not change (p = 0.33), and the S5E correlation is not significant (R = -0.010, p = 0.82). Sextiles 2 and 4 also increase (p = 0.015 and 5.7e-4). Reading b (arousals of 40 to 120 s) gives no top-sextile increase. DANDI agrees under reading a (26 triplets, p = 0.024, 0.13, R = -0.011).

fig5c-wake-movement¶

WAKE periods with more movement have a larger effect on the rate increase of the fastest sextile from one packet to the next (R = 0.43).

Source: Results, Sleep sub-states induce differential lasting firing rate changes, paragraph 3; Figure 5C, upper left, and legend. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

In [52]:
for ds in DS:
    for wr in "ab":
        x1, x2, x3, y, cover = [], [], [], [], []; skipped = 0
        for s in D[ds]:
            cells = s["E"][s["sextile"] == 5]
            if len(cells) == 0 or not s["cycles"]:
                skipped += len(triplets(s, "NWN", wr)) if s["cycles"] else 0
                continue
            G = s["G"]; k = W.secs(W.state_pieces(s, "nrem"))
            mo = G.get("motion"); emg = G.get("emg")
            thr = np.nanmean(mo[k]) + 5 * np.nanstd(mo[k]) if mo is not None else np.nan
            for a, b, c in triplets(s, "NWN", wr):
                kk = W.secs([b])
                ch = np.nanmean(W.cell_rates(s, [c], cells)[0] - W.cell_rates(s, [a], cells)[0])
                m_ = mo[kk] if mo is not None else np.full(len(kk), np.nan)
                cover.append((s["name"], int(b[0]), int(b[1]), int(np.isfinite(m_).sum()), len(kk),
                               len(s["motion"]) if "motion" in s else 0))
                x1.append(np.nanmean(m_) if np.isfinite(m_).any() else np.nan)
                x2.append(np.nanmean(m_[np.isfinite(m_)] > thr) if np.isfinite(m_).any() else np.nan)
                x3.append(np.nanmean(emg[kk]) if emg is not None and np.isfinite(emg[kk]).any() else np.nan)
                y.append(ch)
        if len(y) < 3:
            pr(f"== {ds} reading {wr}: {len(y)} triplets; not tested (no motion or EMG signal)" if ds == "000041" else f"== {ds} reading {wr}: {len(y)} triplets"); continue
        x1, x2, x3, y = map(np.array, (x1, x2, x3, y))
        pr(f"== {ds} reading {wr}: {len(y)} triplets in sessions with a top-sextile pE cell; {skipped} more in sessions without one, left out")
        if wr == "a":
            nomo = [c_ for c_ in cover if c_[3] == 0]
            pr(f"== {ds} reading a: {len(cover)} triplets, {len(nomo)} with no motion sample in their WAKE; for those, (session, WAKE start, end, "
               f"seconds with motion, seconds of WAKE, length of the session's _Motion in s): {nomo}")
        for nm, x in [("(a) mean motion", x1), ("(b) fraction above 5 SD of nonREM", x2), ("(c) mean EMG", x3)]:
            ok = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
            r = stats.pearsonr(x[ok], y[ok]) if ok.sum() > 2 else (np.nan, np.nan)
            pr(f"== {ds} WAKE reading {wr}, {nm}: R={r[0]:.3f} p={fmt(r[1])} n={ok.sum()}")
        # motion where it covers the WAKE, EMG where it does not (reading c is for a missing motion signal)
        xm = np.where(np.isfinite(x1), (x1 - np.nanmean(x1)) / np.nanstd(x1), (x3 - np.nanmean(x3)) / np.nanstd(x3))
        ok = np.isfinite(xm) & np.isfinite(y)
        if ok.sum() > 2:
            r = stats.pearsonr(xm[ok], y[ok]); pr(f"   {ds} reading {wr}, z-scored motion, EMG where motion is missing: R={r[0]:.3f} p={fmt(r[1])} n={ok.sum()}")

The top sextile's change does not correlate with movement during WAKE (mean motion R = 0.222, p = 0.36; fraction above threshold R = -0.139, p = 0.57; reading b R = -0.079 and 0.008). Mean EMG, the criterion's reading for a dataset without motion, gives R = 0.550, p = 0.015 on these 19, a variant on CRCNS, which has motion. DANDI holds neither motion nor EMG, and its only ElectricalSeries is the 1250 Hz LFP, so the claim could not be tested there.

fig5c-rem-duration¶

Longer REM episodes produce a proportionally larger decrease of rates from one packet to the next, across all sextiles (R = -0.22).

for ds in DS:
    xa, ya, yb, xc, yc = [], [], [], [], []
    for s in D[ds]:
        if len(s["E"]) == 0: continue
        for a, b, c in triplets(s, "NRN"):
            r0 = W.cell_rates(s, [a], s["E"])[0]; r1 = W.cell_rates(s, [c], s["E"])[0]
            dur = b[1] - b[0]
            xa.append(dur); ya.append(np.nanmean(r1) - np.nanmean(r0))
            ok = r0 > 0; yb.append(np.nanmean((r1[ok] - r0[ok]) / r0[ok]) if ok.any() else np.nan)
            ok2 = (r0 > 0) & (r1 > 0); xc += [dur] * ok2.sum(); yc += list(np.log10(r1[ok2]) - np.log10(r0[ok2]))
    xa, ya, yb = map(np.array, (xa, ya, yb))
    ra = stats.pearsonr(xa, ya); ok = np.isfinite(yb); rb = stats.pearsonr(xa[ok], yb[ok]); rc = stats.pearsonr(xc, yc)
    pr(f"== {ds}: REM duration against (a) mean-rate change R={ra[0]:.3f} p={fmt(ra[1])} n={len(xa)}; (b) mean relative change R={rb[0]:.3f} p={fmt(rb[1])}; "
       f"(c) per cell log change R={rc[0]:.3f} p={fmt(rc[1])} n={len(xc)}")

fig5c-delta-change-slow-cells¶

Regardless of the intervening state, the increase of the slowest sextile from packet n to n+1 correlates positively with the change in delta power between the packets; the same is not found for the fastest sextile.

for ds in DS:
    for b_ in ["delta", "delta14"]:
        res = []
        for q in (0, 5):
            x, y = [], []
            for s in D[ds]:
                cells = s["E"][s["sextile"] == q]
                if "bpn_" + b_ not in s["G"] or len(cells) == 0: continue
                for c in s["cycles"]:
                    pk = c["packets"]
                    for p0, p1 in zip(pk[:-1], pk[1:]):
                        x.append(W.gmean(s, "bpn_" + b_, [p1]) - W.gmean(s, "bpn_" + b_, [p0]))
                        y.append(np.nanmean(W.cell_rates(s, [p1], cells)[0] - W.cell_rates(s, [p0], cells)[0]))
            x, y = np.array(x), np.array(y); ok = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
            r = stats.pearsonr(x[ok], y[ok]); res.append(f"{'slowest' if q==0 else 'fastest'} R={r[0]:.3f} p={fmt(r[1])} n={ok.sum()}")
        pr(f"== {ds} {b_}: " + "; ".join(res))

for ds in DS:
    for r in "ab":
        A, B, Ab, Bb = [], [], [], []
        for s in D[ds]:
            fa, la = [], []
            for c in s["cycles"]:
                if len(c["packets"]) < 2 or len(s["I"]) == 0: continue
                f = W.cell_rates(s, c["packets"][:1], s["I"])[0]; l = W.cell_rates(s, c["packets"][-1:], s["I"])[0]
                A.append(f); B.append(l); fa.append(f); la.append(l)
            if fa: Ab.append(np.mean(fa, 0)); Bb.append(np.mean(la, 0))
        x, y = (np.concatenate(A), np.concatenate(B)) if r == "a" else (np.concatenate(Ab), np.concatenate(Bb))
        lx, ly, drop = W.log_pairs(x, y); o = W.ols_slope(lx, ly); rv = W.ols_slope(ly, lx)
        pr(f"== {ds} reading {r}: pI log10 slope last on first {o['slope']:.4f} [{o['lo']:.4f}, {o['hi']:.4f}], R={o['R']:.3f}, n={o['n']} (dropped {drop}); "
           f"reverse, first on last, {rv['slope']:.4f} [{rv['lo']:.4f}, {rv['hi']:.4f}]; mean log10 change {np.mean(ly - lx):+.4f}, signed-rank p={fmt(stats.wilcoxon(ly, lx).pvalue)}")

Result: not reproduced. The pI log slope from first to last packet is below 1 with its 95% interval excluding 1: CRCNS 0.836 [0.766, 0.906] (reading a) and 0.888 [0.802, 0.973] (b). The reverse slope is also below 1 (0.892 and 0.876) and pI rates fall from first to last packet (mean log10 change -0.054, signed-rank p = 6.7e-4), so the interval excludes 1 partly by regression to the mean and partly by a decrease. DANDI: 0.917 [0.838, 0.995] and 0.790 [0.660, 0.920].

sleep-homogenizes-rates¶

The net effect of sleep is to homogenize the firing rate distribution, fast cells decreasing and slow cells increasing, so the population rate dispersion falls.

Source: Discussion, paragraph 1; Figure 6 and legend. The criterion and its readings are in the claims file; the code below runs each reading it names.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

Outcomes are judged on CRCNS:fcx-1; the DANDI:000041 result of each claim is in its section.

Of 53 claims, 27 reproduced, 10 partially reproduced, 16 not reproduced, 0 blocked.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. Outcomes rest on CRCNS:fcx-1, with the lab's deposited intervals, UP/DOWN states and spindles. On DANDI the WAKE, SLEEP, packet, MA and episode intervals are built from the Awake, Non-REM and REM epochs, and UP/DOWN states and spindles are detected here. Band power uses 2 s windows every 1 s (averaged to 10 s where the paper's 10 s window applies) and, within UP states, 200 ms windows every 100 ms (an assumption). ISIs for the burst index are counted from spike times within each state interval. Rates and counts in normalized-time bins use the 1 s grid, each second going to the bin that holds its centre; the REM part of figs5-within-wake-rem also uses exact spike times. Where the paper leaves a sampling unit, normalization or test open, every reading the claims file names is run and printed. Where a criterion counts parts that "hold", a part holds when it meets M4's reproduced level (an assumption; the result with p < 0.05 is shown too). Sextile tests on WAKE are also run with the cells ranked on WAKE without the windows tested, and rate-rate slopes are shown with their reverse regressions, as checks on regression to the mean.

What was found about the datasets. CRCNS:fcx-1 holds the paper's data set in full and its deposited intervals and detections reproduce Table S1, except the WAKE-SLEEP duration (median 4214 s against the 5918 s Table S1 prints) and the microarousals: its MA list holds 2130 MAs, of which 434 lie within SLEEP and 1670 outside any scored SLEEP or WAKE, against 790 in the paper. DANDI:000041 lacks 5 of the 27 sessions (rat B22 and two Dino ACC probes), has no LFP for Dino-061914, holds only Awake, Non-REM and REM states (no WAKE-SLEEP cycles, packets, MAs, UP/DOWN states or spindles), no motion or EMG signal and no wideband signal, and its cell-type labels and unit sets differ from the lab's CRCNS files in several sessions. The DANDI LFP starts at time 0 in every file, and its delta power is higher in nonREM than in WAKE as scored.
